fields: Do Not Start With This When

rows.Method Family: Allele-specific copy number and phylogeography inference
rows.Main Input: SRT transcript counts + allele counts at germline SNPs + spatial coordinates from one or more slices
rows.Main Use in This Topic: infer allele-specific CNAs, clone labels, tumor phylogeography, and optional tumor proportion from SRT
rows.Main Output: allele-specific copy-number profiles + clone labels + phylogeny/phylogeography
rows.Key Difference: Uses allele-specific read information to identify CNLOH and mirrored subclonal CNAs and links inferred clones to phylogeography, rather than relying on total expression-only CNA profiles.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Methods method paper, PMC code availability reports the official GitHub and Zenodo code, and the paper validates against matched WES-derived allele-specific copy numbers. Closest-alternative and scale labels are Layer 2 synthesized judgment.
rows.Best First Choice When: When SRT data include usable allele counts and the analysis goal is allele-specific CNA clone inference or spatial tumor phylogeography.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When only expression totals are available, allele-specific events are not part of the question, or a point-mutation clone deconvolution model is required.

rows.Main Input: single-cell or spatial omic copy-number profiles, with optional matched bulk DNA sequencing prior information
rows.Main Use in This Topic: detect cancer subclones, label malignant cells or spots, and trace spatially segregated subclones using copy-number profiles
rows.Main Output: subclone assignments + malignant labels + traced spatial subclone patterns
rows.Key Difference: Targets de novo subclone detection from copy-number profiles across single-cell and spatial data, with optional matched bulk DNA priors, rather than SRT-specific allele-specific phylogeography or sparse Slide-seq binning.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Methods method paper, the publisher abstract states applicability to spatial transcriptomics and single-cell sequencing, and the official GitHub README provides ST tutorials and installation. Resource, comparator, and scale labels are Layer 2 synthesis.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the input already has copy-number profiles or compatible CNA estimates and the goal is subclone detection across spatial or single-cell tumor omics.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the main need is allele-specific CNA phylogeography, somatic point-mutation clone deconvolution, or sparse high-resolution Slide-seq CNA recovery from raw expression.

rows.Main Input: spatial transcriptomics expression matrix + spatial coordinates / spot graph
rows.Main Use in This Topic: infer total-copy-number profiles and spatial clone assignments from ST expression data
rows.Key Difference: Uses an HMM for copy-number profiles and an HMRF for spatial clone assignment from expression and coordinates, making it an ST-only total-CNA baseline rather than an allele-specific or matched-DNA method.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Physical Biology method paper, PMC code availability reports the GitHub implementation, and the paper compares STARCH with non-spatial STARCH and InferCNV on simulated/pseudo-spatial and breast-tissue ST data. Resource and later-method positioning are Layer 2 synthesis.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the available data are ST expression plus coordinates and the intended readout is a coarse total-CNA spatial clone assignment without allele-specific or matched-DNA requirements.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When allele-specific CNAs, point-mutation-defined clones, high-resolution sparse Slide-seq binning, or broad current-method validation are required.

rows.Main Input: ST mutation read counts + clone genotypes from bulk DNA/WES + pathology-image-derived cell counts + expression matrix
rows.Main Use in This Topic: infer clone proportions in each ST spot and clone-specific expression by integrating genomic, image, and spatial transcriptomic data
rows.Main Output: spot-level clone proportions + refined cell counts + clone-specific expression profiles
rows.Key Difference: Deconvolves clone proportions using somatic point-mutation and matched genomic information, whereas most alternatives infer clones from copy-number signal in expression or allele-specific CNA profiles.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Nature Communications method paper, PMC code availability reports the installable package and GitHub repository, and the paper validates simulated and tumor datasets while documenting dependence on WES, H&E-derived cell counts, and ST mutation reads. Comparator and scale cues are Layer 2 synthesis.
rows.Best First Choice When: When matched bulk DNA/WES-derived clone genotypes, ST mutation read evidence, and pathology-derived cell-count priors are available and spot-level clone mixture deconvolution is the main question.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the workflow must use ST expression alone, copy-number-only inference is sufficient, or matched genomic and image-derived inputs are unavailable.

rows.Main Input: sparse Slide-seq-like ST expression data + spatial coordinates + non-malignant reference spots or beads
rows.Main Use in This Topic: detect spatial CNA patterns and potential subclones from high-resolution sparse spatial transcriptomics
rows.Main Output: binned spatial CNA scores + CNA-defined clusters / potential subclone patterns
rows.Key Difference: Uses expression-aware spatial binning to recover CNA signal from sparse high-resolution Slide-seq-like data, rather than modeling Visium-like spots, allele-specific phylogeography, or point-mutation clone mixtures.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed/DOI verify the Genome Biology method paper, PMC data availability reports CRAN, GitHub, analysis vignettes, and Zenodo code deposition, and the paper validates simulated and real Slide-seq-like metastatic breast cancer data against sc/snRNA-seq, InferCNV, CopyKAT, and WES-derived signals. Comparator and scale labels are Layer 2 synthesis.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the data are sparse high-resolution Slide-seq-like ST and the goal is spatial CNA recovery or potential subclone detection through spatial binning.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the data are not Slide-seq-like, allele-specific phylogeography is required, or clone deconvolution should be driven by matched somatic mutation genotypes.
